findings.title: Duplicate self.downsize definition silently overrides 4-arg version
findings.body: Two `self.downsize` methods are defined (lines 145-147 with `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` and lines 149-151 with `(from, to, dimensions, opts)`). In Ruby the second definition replaces the first, so any existing caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` will now pass `height` as the `opts` hash position and raise ArgumentError or build wrong instructions. Use a single method with an optional/flexible signature.

findings.title: Downsize loop can spin without shrinking and ignores failures
findings.body: The loop repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%")` while `tempfile.size` exceeds the limit. `tempfile.size` on an already-opened Tempfile may be cached/stale after the external `convert` rewrites the file on disk (the Ruby File object's size is read via fstat, but the file position/content is replaced out of band), so the check may not reflect the new size. Also the return value of `downsize` is ignored: if `convert` fails, the loop still runs 5 times and the oversized file is then passed to `Upload.create_for`, producing no useful error. Should check the return value and break on failure, and re-stat the path (e.g. `File.size(tempfile.path)`).

findings.title: Downsizing in-place with same source and destination path
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same file as ImageMagick input and output. Converting in place is unreliable (and gifsicle's `--output` to the same file as input is explicitly unsafe), risking a truncated/corrupt upload. Write to a new temp file and swap.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb settings
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` was replaced with a hardcoded `10 * 1024`, discarding the per-type site settings. Attachments (which are not downsized server-side) can now be submitted far above the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` and will be rejected only by the server, and admins who lowered/raised the limits get an inconsistent client-side check and a misleading error message. The same hardcoding at line 246 shows the wrong size in the 413 message.

findings.title: API URL download size cap hardcoded to 10MB
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` no longer respects `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, so API-provided URLs can always pull up to 10MB regardless of site configuration; for non-image files there is no downsizing fallback, so the admin-configured limit is effectively bypassed at download time.
